extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: A comprehensive multimodal dataset consisting of 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT scans (50,188 reconstructed 3D chest CT volumes, totaling over 14.3 million 2D slices) paired with corresponding textual radiology reports from 21,304 unique patients, enriched with multi-abnormality labels for 18 distinct findings.
extraction.creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Chenyu Wang, Furkan Almas, Ayse Gulnihan Simsek, Sewal Nil Esirgun, Irem Dogan, Omer Faruk Durugol, Benjamin Hou, Suprosanna Shit, Weicheng Dai, Murong Xu, Hadrien Reynaud, Muhammed Furkan Dasdelen, Bastian Wittmann, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Enis Simsar, Mehmet Simsar, Emine Bensu Erdemir, Abdullah Alanbay, Anjany Sekuboyina, Berkan Lafci, Ahmet Kaplan, Zhiyong Lu, Malgorzata Polacin, Bernhard Kainz, Christian Bluethgen, Kayhan Batmanghelich, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir, Bjoern Menze
extraction.citeAs: Hamamci, I. E., et al. (2025). Developing generalist foundation models from a multimodal dataset for 3D computed tomography. arXiv:2403.17834v4.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Non-contrast chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports were retrieved from the hospital database of Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, including all reconstructed volumes created using various kernels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For abnormality labeling, conditions not referenced in either the findings or impression sections of the reports were considered absent.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Hospital database of Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, consisting of non-contrast chest CT scans and Turkish radiology text reports.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were de-identified by removing dates and personal identifiers of patients and medical professionals using regular expressions. Reports were translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API and then reviewed, corrected, and verified by bilingual final-year medical students to remove residual identifying information.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Volumes involving contrast material or non-chest regions were excluded. Volume orientation was standardized, and identifying information was removed from metadata. Volumes were resampled to a uniform voxel spacing of 0.75 mm x 0.75 mm x 1.5 mm, then center-cropped or padded to 480x480x240 voxels. CT values were converted to Hounsfield Units (HU) using rescale intercept and slope, clipped to [-1000, 1000], and normalized to [-1, 1].
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 1,000 reports were manually annotated by merging findings and impression sections across 18 distinct abnormalities (grouping similar conditions such as mucoid impactions and lung opacities). These were split into 800 training and 200 validation reports to fine-tune a RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m model, which was subsequently used to automatically extract binary abnormality labels for the remaining 24,692 reports. Anatomical organ segmentations were also generated using a pre-existing segmentation model.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Precision, recall, and F1 scores were evaluated for the fine-tuned RadBERT model on the manual validation set of 200 reports across all 18 abnormalities, demonstrating high classification accuracy (F1 scores ranging from 0.95 to 1.00).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Google Translate API, RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m, TotalSegmentator, Meta Llama 3.1 8B
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Patient age (ranging from 18 to 102 years) and patient sex (41.6% female, 58.4% male)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to advance 3D medical vision-language modeling, reduce radiologist workload, automate diagnostic reporting, and support clinical decision-making where immediate radiological expertise is scarce.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Data originates from a single medical center in Turkey, which may induce institutional or geographic bias. Imaging devices are skewed toward specific manufacturers (61.5% Philips, 30.1% Siemens, 8.4% PNMS). Label extraction and model behavior are also sensitive to reporting language and terminology styles.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Single-institution cohort limited to non-contrast chest CT scans without other anatomical regions or modalities (e.g., MRI, PET). Reports are translated from Turkish to English. Automated report generation performance, while superior to baselines, remains insufficient for standalone clinical deployment and carries risks of hallucination.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and benchmarking of self-supervised, supervised, and multimodal AI foundation models for 3D chest CT analysis, including multi-abnormality zero-shot classification, image-to-image case retrieval, text-to-image retrieval, visual question answering (VQA), and automated radiology report generation.
